# RV power station + solar picks

The right combo depends on whether you need to run a roof A/C. For an RV, check three specs: the **30A RV outlet**, the **solar input ceiling** (a big array is wasted if the unit caps it), and **continuous output**. A 13,500 BTU roof A/C draws about 1,500W running and spikes above 3,000W at startup ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).

## Best by use case

**Full-time or boondocking, running A/C: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge, expandable past 12kWh.
- About 0-80% in roughly 50 minutes from a wall outlet.
- It's heavy (a two-person lift) and the priciest option once you add batteries.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy RV comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/). Prices weren't listed there, so check the "Check price" link on that page.

**Best mid-range value: BLUETTI AC200L**
- 2,048Wh, 2,400W, a built-in 30A RV outlet, and up to 1,200W of solar input.
- About 62 lb.
- Sources: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) and [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/).

**Big capacity for the money: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- 3,456Wh, 3,600W at 120V, an RV outlet, and up to 2,000W of solar input across three inputs. You need panels on all three inputs to reach that, since each takes 650W max.
- 45 kg, so it's not hand-portable, and it has a 5-year warranty.
- The store price is $1,499. Code EXTRA12 (12% off orders over $1,200) brings it to about $1,319 and expires 2026-11-15. Code ALLPOWERS26 (10% off) brings it to about $1,349 and expires 2026-12-30. Stores usually allow one code per order.
- [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) (affiliate link, so the site earns a commission). Details: [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh).

**Weekends, lights, fridge, Starlink, no A/C: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus or Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**
- The DELTA 3 Plus is 1,024Wh with up to 1,000W of solar input, about 28 lb, and expandable to 5kWh.
- The Jackery 1000 v2 is 1,070Wh, about 23.8 lb, and caps solar at 400W. It pairs easily with SolarSaga 100W and 200W panels.
- Source: [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/).

## Solar panels
- Two 200W panels fully use a 400W-capped unit like the Jackery 1000 v2.
- For 2,000Wh-class units, a 300-400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of good sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- One guide suggests the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase for lighter setups ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)).
- Match panel voltage and current to the unit's solar input limits before buying.

My search results didn't include direct purchase links for specific panels. The review pages above link to current listings.

## Caveats
- Specs and prices vary between these review sites, and several are affiliate-driven. Confirm on the manufacturer's page before buying.
- Hardwiring a power station into your RV's shore inlet may call for an electrician. A TT-30 adapter works for plug-in use.

To narrow it down, tell me whether you'll run the A/C, how many days you'll go without hookups, and your budget.
